sentences.text: Ms. Bhagyashree Gupta, learned counsel for the appell  Shri Akshansh Mehra, learned counsel for the responde  ORDER
The appellants have filed this appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act being aggrieved by the award dated 13.8.2019 passed in Claim Case No.171/2018 challenging the quantum of compensation.

2. Short facts giving rise to the case are that on 30.6.2018 when deceased Manish was going on his motorcycle having registration No.MP-09-MG-2569 to Dharampuri, when he reached near Gulati Petrol Pump driver of Dumper Truck No.MP-09-GF-2988 came driving the same in very rash and negligent manner from the side of Khalghat and directly dashed into the motorcycle of deceased Manish from behind resulting in grievous injuries on his body.
He succumbed to the injuries on the spot itself.
2.1 The appellants/claimants filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the death of Manish.

The claims Tribunal after considering the evidence as brought on record by the parties concluded that the appellants were entitled for compensation of Rs.6,00,600/- for loss of dependency, Rs.15,000/- was awarded for funeral expenses and loss of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17349 2 MA-848-2020 estate .
Thus, total compensation of Rs.6,30,600/- was awarded.
3. Counsel for the appellant submits that the deceased was earning Rs.15,000/- per month at the time of accident.
She refers to the statement of Govind (AW-1), who has stated that his son Manish was 22 years of age, was earning Rs.22,000/- per month as he was working as Driver.
The claims Tribunal disbelieved the statement of AW-1 without any reason.

She further submits that witness Rahul (AW-2) has also stated that Manish was working for him and was driving a private Omni Bus having registration No.MP-07-BA-1278 for which was paying Rs.15,000/- per month to Manish.

Thus, by disbelieving the same, income of the deceased was taken on notional basis.
She submits that this finding of the Tribunal is not in accordance with the evidence available on record.
She also submits that no amount has been awarded for loss of consortium.

She further submits that claims Tribunal while assessing quantum of compensation applied the multiplier of 13 by taking age of the mother and not of the deceased, which is not correct in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 and in the case of National Insurance Co.Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and others , reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 .

sentences.text: She submits that multiplier of 18 would apply.
She accordingly prays for enhancement of compensation.
4. Per contra , counsel for the respondent/Insurance Company submits that the claims Tribunal has rightly taken income of the deceased @ Rs.5,500/- per month by treating him unskilled Labour.

He submits that although, AW-1 and AW-2 deposed before the Tribunal that the deceased was earning Rs.15,000/- per NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:17349 3 MA-848-2020 month, but not even a single document has been produced on record.
Thus, the conclusion drawn by the claims Tribunal is correct and does not warrant any interference.
As regards the multiplier he submits that in view of the fact that deceased was 26 years of age multiplier of 17 would apply and not a multiplier of 5.
Heard learned counsel for the parties, perused the record.

6. From findings contained in para 16 and 17 of the award it is clear that the appellants were not able to bring on record any material to show that the deceased was employed as Driver for Rahul (AW-2).
Mere statement of father of the deceased and AW-2 cannot be taken to be a gospel truth.
Thus, no interference in this regard discarding the statements of AW-1 and AW-2 is warranted.

However, the claims Tribunal while treating the deceased as unskilled Labour has taken his income @ Rs.5,500/-
per month.
At the relevant time i.e.on the date of accident 30.6.2018 the notional income of an unskilled Labour in terms of the guidelines issued by M.P.State Legal Services Authority is Rs.7,325/- per month.

Thus, in the considered view of this Court and the law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Hans Raj Vs. Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd., passed in SLP (C)
No.3511 of 2020, income of the deceased is taken at Rs.7,325/- per month.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. As regards the multiplier the claims Tribunal has applied multiplier of 13 by taking into account the age of the mother, which is not correct in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma and Pranay Sethi (supra).
By considering age of the deceased at 26 the multiplier of 17 would be applicable as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma (supra).

As such after above modifications the compensation for loss of dependency would come to Rs.10,46,010/-.
8.

It is seen that the claims Tribunal has not awarded anything for loss of NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:17349 4 MA-848-2020 consortium as there are two appellants/claimants, who are father and mother of the deceased.

Thus, they are entitled for filial consortium in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co.Ltd. Vs. Nanu Govind vs Dilip on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75046118/
2 Ram, reported in 2019 ACJ 2782 .

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, they are awarded Rs.40,000/- each for the same.
For funeral expenses and loss of estate correct amount has been awarded by the claims Tribunal.
Now thus, the total amount of compensation comes to Rs.11,56,010/-.
The claims Tribunal has already awarded Rs.6,30,600/-.
Thus, the appellants are now entitled for payment of Rs.5,25,410/- over and above what has already been awarded by the claims Tribunal.
The enhanced amount would carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of application till its payment.
The appellants have valued this appeal at Rs.2,50,000/-.
Thus, they are directed to pay the deficit Court fees within a period of one month from today.
9. With the above modifications the present appeal is partly allowed and disposed off.
